transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. How can I help you today?

Hi, yes, thank you for seeing me. Um, so I guess what brings me in is this constant restless feeling I’ve been having. It’s like I’m wound just way too tight and I can’t fully settle down, even when I’m supposed to be doing something calm. 

Like, if I'm sitting through a planning meeting at work... which, honestly, those meetings have been dragging on forever lately because our spring inventory is completely delayed. Trying to get the new seasonal lines sorted out with our overseas vendors has been a total nightmare. The shipping costs alone are ridiculous right now, and I swear I spend half my day just tracking crates on my computer. 

But anyway, even outside of work, I can't settle. Like when I'm painting, or trying to do yoga. I actually just went to this new yoga studio on 4th street last week—the one next to the bakery? They make you leave your shoes in this little cubby outside the main room, which makes sense, but the bamboo floors in there are absolutely freezing, so I spent half the class just wishing I had brought grip socks. But yeah, even in situations like that where I'm supposed to be perfectly calm, I just have this restless energy I can't shake.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, relationships, or other responsibilities, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

No, not really. I mean, I don't just sit and worry if there's nothing actually wrong. If there's a fire to put out at work, I deal with it, but I wouldn't call myself a worrier. 

Not like my sister, anyway. She worries about absolutely everything. She called me on Tuesday completely panicking about her dog's diet. She has this golden doodle, Buster, and she buys him this incredibly expensive grain-free kibble. Which, honestly, I was reading an article just the other day about how grain-free diets might actually be linked to heart issues in dogs? I don't even have a dog, but it popped up on my news feed while I was trying to find a recipe for lemon caper chicken. I ended up just making salmon anyway because the chicken breasts at the grocery store looked really bruised, which is happening a lot lately. I feel like the produce and meat quality is just tanking everywhere, probably because of all the supply chain stuff I was talking about earlier. 

But um... wait, what was the question? Oh, worrying. Yeah, no, my mind doesn't really get stuck on worrying about things unless there's a real issue staring me in the face.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, pacing, or feeling physically unable to stay still, even when you're not particularly stressed or anxious?

Oh, absolutely. Like, when I'm on video calls with our suppliers, my foot is usually just bouncing away under the desk. And I don't even realize I'm doing it at first. I'm usually clicking a pen or twisting my ring around so much that I actually have to mute myself so they don't hear the clicking on the microphone, or I have to consciously move my hands out of view of the camera. 

Which is kind of funny because I am obsessed with the specific pens I use—they're those Pilot G2s, but specifically the 0.38 millimeter ultra-fine ones? You can't really find that exact size at regular office supply stores anymore, so I have to order them in bulk from this warehouse site. Last time I accidentally ordered the blue ink instead of black, and it completely threw off my entire color-coding system for my inventory planner. I still use a physical paper planner because the digital ones just... I don't know, if I don't write it down with a real pen, it doesn't exist to me. Plus, the paper quality in the one I get from Japan is just incredible, no bleed-through at all. 

But um... yeah, if I'm sitting there, even if it's a totally normal, low-stress call about shipping delays or whatever, I'm definitely clicking or bouncing or twisting something. I just can't stay perfectly still.
Do you find that you often feel tired or that you don't have much energy, even if you haven't been doing anything particularly physically or mentally taxing?

No, I wouldn't say I feel tired. Honestly, it's usually the opposite, I just have all this energy. I actually tried cutting back on my coffee last month just to see if that would help me settle down a bit. I usually walk to this little cafe about four blocks from my office—they use this specific brand of barista-blend oat milk that foams up perfectly. Most oat milks totally separate and get weirdly watery when you pour them into hot espresso, which just ruins the whole texture of the drink. 

I actually tried to order a wholesale case of that exact oat milk for my house through one of my distributor contacts, but the shipping box got completely crushed in transit. Dealing with damaged freight has been such a massive headache this entire quarter. Our warehouse manager, Dave, was just complaining to me yesterday that the shrink wrap they’ve been using on the pallets lately is way too flimsy, so everything just shifts around on the delivery trucks... 

But um, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, having low energy. Yeah, no, I don't really ever feel drained or tired like that.
Do you often find it hard to focus or stay attentive, even during tasks or activities that most people would consider straightforward or routine?

No, not really. I don't have trouble focusing on things, especially if I'm busy. Like, if I'm reviewing purchase orders or negotiating with vendors, I'm totally dialed in. Actually, I was just negotiating a new contract with our packaging supplier last week. They tried to raise their prices on the corrugated boxes by like, fifteen percent, which is completely ridiculous. I told their rep, Sarah—she's new, she took over for Tom who retired last spring and moved to Arizona. Or maybe it was New Mexico? Somewhere hot and dry because his wife has terrible arthritis. 

Anyway, I told Sarah that we could easily switch to a different manufacturer if they didn't honor our previous rate. There's this other company based out of Ohio that's been trying to get our business for years. They sent us this promotional box full of their sample materials, and inside, they packed it with these gourmet chocolate truffles instead of packing peanuts. Which was a really clever marketing trick, honestly, but the chocolate melted a little in transit and got all over this really nice glossy brochure they included. I felt kind of bad throwing it away, but you can't really save a chocolate-smeared pamphlet. 

But um... what were we talking about? Focusing? Yeah, no, I don't really have a hard time staying on task. If there's work to do, I just get it done.
Looking back at your childhood, do you remember having similar experiences with restlessness, trouble staying still, or difficulty focusing during school or other activities?

Oh, definitely. I mean, my mom actually kept all my old report cards in this massive plastic bin in her basement. It's one of those heavy-duty storage tubs, the kind with the yellow latching lids? They're supposed to be totally waterproof, which is good because her basement flooded a few years ago when the sump pump failed during that huge spring storm. It was a complete disaster, she had to rip up all the carpet and ended up replacing it with this really nice luxury vinyl plank flooring that looks exactly like weathered oak. It's so much easier to clean, honestly. 

But yeah, she pulled out that bin recently, and reading through those old notes from my elementary school teachers was hilarious. They were always sending notes home saying I couldn't stay in my chair. Like, I was constantly popping out of my seat, or I'd be talking over the other kids. And I was terrible about blurting out answers—I'd just rush to answer before the teacher even finished asking the question. 

Actually, I still kind of do that sometimes in vendor meetings when I know exactly where they're going with a pitch. Like this one guy last month who was trying to sell us on this new inventory tracking software. He was taking forever to get to the pricing structure, and I just... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Childhood stuff? Yeah, the restlessness and talking out of turn was definitely a thing back then too.
